narrative.title: The Compiler's Rearrangement Desk
narrative.scenario: A calculator firmware evaluates expressions on a stack machine that wants operators after their operands, yet engineers type expressions the human way with operators in between and parentheses overriding precedence. The firmware's translation desk rewrites each expression so that `a + b` becomes `a b +` while honoring that `^` outranks `*` and `/`, which outrank `+` and `-`.
narrative.inputFormat: A string expression in infix form using single alphanumeric operands, the operators + - * / ^, and parentheses.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the equivalent postfix (Reverse Polish) expression as a string.
constraints: Operands are single letters or digits

testCases.explanation: Parenthesized sub-expressions are resolved first, then multiplication/addition levels unwrap per precedence.
B+C emits first; * then / follow, and equal precedence pops left-to-right.

hintLevels: Level 1: Operands go straight to output; operators wait on a stack until something of lower rank arrives.
Level 2: A closing parenthesis flushes the stack back to its matching opener; end of input flushes everything.
Level 3: Pop while the stack top has greater-or-equal precedence — the equal case preserves left-to-right evaluation.
